name: DriveTrack
description: This paper presents DriveTrack, a new benchmark and data generation framework for long-range keypoint tracking in real-world videos. DriveTrack is motivated by the observation that the accuracy of state-of-the-art trackers depends strongly on visual attributes around the selected keypoints, such as texture and lighting. The problem is that these artifacts are especially pronounced in real-world videos, but these trackers are unable to train on such scenes due to a dearth of annotations. DriveTrack bridges this gap by building a framework to automatically annotate point tracks on autonomous driving datasets. We release a dataset consisting of 1 billion point tracks across 24 hours of video, which is seven orders of magnitude greater than prior real-world benchmarks and on par with the scale of synthetic benchmarks. DriveTrack unlocks new use cases for point tracking in real-world videos. First, we show that fine-tuning keypoint trackers on DriveTrack improves accuracy on real-world scenes by up to 7%. Second, we analyze the sensitivity of trackers to visual artifacts in real scenes and motivate the idea of running assistive keypoint selectors alongside trackers.
evaluation_method: tracking accuracy / percentage of correctly tracked keypoints and endpoint error; improvements often reported as % accuracy gain after fine-tuning
general_score_metric: tracking_accuracy (percentage of correctly tracked keypoints) and tracking_endpoint_error
reputation: A large-scale, recent benchmark (1 billion tracks) expected to be influential for real-world keypoint/point-tracking research in autonomous driving.
notes: Automatically annotated at scale so labels may contain noise; domain-specific to driving scenes (potential distributional biases); very large and compute-intensive to process; non-LLM benchmark.
